findings.trigger: SparseCoSENTLoss is used with a SparseEncoder that does not have a 'similarity_fn_name' attribute or when the parent CoSENTLoss.__init__ expects a Transformer model, not a SparseEncoder
findings.consequence: The code sets model.similarity_fn_name = 'cosine' but this attribute is not part of the SparseEncoder interface and the parent CoSENTLoss expects a model with sentence_embedding_dimension etc. The base CoSENTLoss.__init__ will fail or produce wrong loss because the SparseEncoder does not have the required attributes (e.g., get_sentence_embedding_dimension). The override only sets a non-existent attribute and then calls super().__init__ which will raise AttributeError or produce incorrect loss if the model lacks standard transformer properties. The forward method raises an AttributeError but that is intended; the defect is that the constructor is broken for the intended usage.
